name: Marsh & McLennan Companies, Inc. (brand: Marsh; NYSE: MRSH; ex-MMC)

corporate_actions.event: Announced brand change from Marsh McLennan to 'Marsh' effective January 2026; Business and Client Services (BCS) unit created

NYSE ticker changed from MMC to MRSH (announced 29-Dec-2025). Legal name (Marsh & McLennan Companies, Inc.) and CUSIP unchanged; ISIN therefore unchanged (US5717481023 is derived from CUSIP 571748102 - ISIN not separately re-confirmed in this pass). Project file id kept as MMC.
Agreed to acquire Wilshire (investment consulting); terms not disclosed; bolt-on, not transformational

geography.fx_notes: PitchBook/Morningstar profile: 'about half of its revenue is generated outside the US'. Exact 10-K split not extracted in this pass (not disclosed here, not zero). Q3-26: Risk US&Canada +4% underlying, International +6% (EMEA +7%, APAC +4%, LatAm flat).

kpis.name: Q3-26 underlying growth: Risk / Reinsurance / People&Investments / Mgmt Consulting
Marsh Global Insurance Market Index: primary commercial rates
kpis.value: -5% (Q3-26) after -6% (Q2-26); global property -10%; US excess casualty +13%

kpis.name: Gross debt / EBITDA (provider)
kpis.value: ~3.1x (PitchBook TTM 3Q2026 total debt $22.3bn incl. leases / EBITDA $7.2bn); ~2.8x using company total debt $20.5bn

kpis.name: Thrive cost programme
kpis.value: Savings target raised $400m -> $600m; ~$750m cost to achieve; actions largely by end-2028

acquisitions.notes: McGriff Insurance Services acquired Nov-2024 (widely reported ~$7.75bn; NOT re-verified in this pass - lead agent to confirm from 10-K). Gap between FY25 reported (+10%) and underlying (+4%) growth largely McGriff.

management.cfo_since: 2016 (CFO); COO role added later - dates not re-verified
management.senior_turnover_5y: Orderly: Dan Glaser -> John Doyle (internal) Jan-2023; business CEOs reshuffled under rebrand (Nick Studer Risk, Dean Klisura Reinsurance, Pat Tomlinson People&Investments, Ted Moynihan Mgmt Consulting)
management.guidance_record: FY26 guide 'underlying growth similar to 2025, margin expansion, solid adj EPS growth' maintained through Q3-26; 18 consecutive years of margin expansion claimed in press coverage

guidance.value: similar to 2025 (FY25: 4%), margin expansion, solid adj EPS growth
~$5.5bn across dividends, M&A and buybacks ($2bn buybacks 9M)

evidence: Reinsurance client retention 'high 90s' (S2)
Mix: RIS ~2/3 of revenue (recurring broking), Consulting ~1/3 incl. more discretionary Oliver Wyman (S2)
A.rationale: Broking/benefits revenue is renewal-based but Oliver Wyman (~$3.9bn run-rate) is project/success-fee driven.

evidence: Largest global broker; 93% of London wholesale trading digital via own platforms (S2)
Retained clients through soft cycles (reinsurance retention high 90s) (S2)
B.rationale: Global placement scale, data and specialist teams create real switching costs for large risks.

evidence: Adj operating margin 28.1% 9M-26 with RIS 33.2% (S2)
Margin expansion reported for many consecutive years (S4)
C.rationale: Scale shows up in sustained margin expansion and capacity facilities (Nimbus/Stratus), though peers have similar margins.

evidence: Primary commercial rates -5% in Q3-26 (S2)
D.rationale: Mid-single-digit runway; pricing cycle now a headwind, new business must carry growth.

evidence: About half of revenue generated outside the US (S1)
International Risk +6% vs US/Canada +4% in Q3-26 (S2)
E.rationale: Balanced developed-market spread; US the largest single country (~half).

evidence: Internal CEO succession 2023; FY guidance reiterated through 2026 (S2)
Greensill litigation settled with $144m charge in Q3-26 (S2)
F.rationale: Delivers guidance with orderly succession; legacy litigation now closed.

evidence: $2bn buybacks + $607m M&A 9M-26; $5.5bn deployment plan (S2)
McGriff (2024) integrated; leverage ~2.8-3.1x (S1,S2)
G.rationale: Balanced deployment with moderate leverage; McGriff returns not yet separately evidenced.

evidence: Widely held, no controlling holder (S1)
H.rationale: Standard large-cap governance; pay/board not reviewed in this pass (low confidence).

evidence: Broker WorkBench cut London placement time from 2-4 weeks to hours (S2)
Consulting AI work is a growth driver but also exposed to AI substitution (S2)
I1.rationale: Large-risk advice and placement are judgement/relationship-heavy, but consulting and benefits admin are more automatable - moderate overall (INFERENCE).

evidence: Digital infrastructure cited as a growth driver; Stratus $10bn property facility for data centres (S2)
I2.rationale: Some revenue linked to data-centre build-out placements; not quantified, judged <5% (INFERENCE).

evidence: Thrive savings raised to $600m citing BCS and technology (S2)
I3.rationale: Large people cost base addressable by AI/automation.

evidence: Commission/fee mix; fiduciary and fee pricing negotiated by large clients (INFERENCE)
I4.rationale: Commission-based pay is not cost-plus, but large clients will push to share productivity gains.

evidence: Rates -5% yet Risk still grew 5% underlying in Q3-26 (S2)
Fiduciary income falling with rates ($100m Q3, -$9m y/y) (S2)
J.rationale: Diversified across broking/consulting; modest sensitivity to pricing cycle and interest rates.

evidence: Q3-26 'noteworthy items' $170m incl. Thrive $71m and Greensill $144m (S2)
K.rationale: Recurring restructuring add-backs (Thrive) mean adjusted > GAAP each year; otherwise clean.

ai.notes: Digital-infrastructure placements (Stratus/Nimbus) and Oliver Wyman AI work are growth drivers; revenue share not disclosed. Judged well below G5 threshold (INFERENCE).

sector_specific.organic_ex_rate_note: INFERENCE: Q3-26 Risk +5% underlying with Marsh index rates -5% (index skews to large accounts; US -1%). Management attributes growth to new business (very high single-digit new business growth in UK/International) and retention; rate contribution likely ~0 to slightly negative in 2026 vs +2-4pts in 2022-24. Reinsurance -1% 9M-26 is the clearest rate drag (property cat).
sector_specific.retention_pct: Reinsurance 'high 90s' (2026); Risk retention not quantified in source
sector_specific.contingent_consideration: not disclosed in sources used (10-K note not extracted)
sector_specific.producer_retention: Not quantified; management says it is 'hiring producers at a higher rate' funded by Thrive (S2)

gates.notes: G1: gross debt/EBITDA ~2.8x (company debt) to 3.1x (PitchBook incl. leases) < 4.0x. G2: Greensill litigation settled Q3-26; no restatement. G4 not computed here (lead agent FCF); broker cash conversion historically high. G6: Wilshire is a small bolt-on; MRSH is acquirer, not target. Ticker change MMC->MRSH effective 14-Jan-2026 is cosmetic.

bull_points: Most diversified global broker/consultant; underlying growth held at 4-5% even with commercial rates falling 5-6%.
Thrive ($600m savings) plus BCS shared services supports continued margin expansion and producer hiring.
Consistent capital return ($5.5bn deployment 2026) with moderate leverage.
bear_points: Soft market: property rates -10% and reinsurance revenue -1% 9M-26; a deeper cycle could take underlying growth to low single digits.
Oliver Wyman (management consulting) is discretionary and success-fee driven; AI could compress consulting and benefits-admin fees.
Falling interest rates cut fiduciary income (~$400m/yr) which drops almost fully to profit.
thesis_breakers: Underlying revenue growth < 3% for two consecutive years.
Adjusted operating margin declines y/y (ending the multi-year expansion record).
Gross debt/EBITDA > 3.5x from a large debt-funded deal.
